question: When is Maha Shivaratri celebrated according to the Drik Panchang?
solution:
The correct answer is **Phalguna****, Krishna Paksha, Chaturdashi.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **Drik Panchang**

 
 
• Drik Panchang is a comprehensive online Hindu almanac that provides detailed astrological and calendar-related information.
 
• It is used to determine auspicious dates and times for various Hindu religious practices and rituals.
 
• Drik Panchang includes data on festivals, vrat (fasting) dates, and other important Hindu events.
 
• It uses precise astronomical calculations to provide daily panchang details like tithi (lunar day), nakshatra (constellation), yoga, karana, and vara (weekday).
 
• The platform also offers tools to calculate muhurat (auspicious time) for various ceremonies like weddings and housewarming events.
 
• Drik Panchang covers multiple Hindu calendars such as the Vikram Samvat and Shaka Samvat.
 
• The website and app are available in multiple languages to cater to a wide audience.
 
• It also includes predictive astrology features like horoscopes and horoscope matching for marriage.
 
• The panchang is updated regularly to reflect accurate sunrise, sunset, moonrise, and moonset times for different locations.
 
• Drik Panchang is widely used by Hindus around the world for both religious and everyday planning.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Maha Shivaratri**

 
 
• Maha Shivaratri is a major Hindu festival dedicated to Lord Shiva, one of the primary deities in Hinduism.
 
• It is celebrated annually on the 14th night of the new moon during the waning phase in the Hindu month of Phalguna or Magha, which typically falls in February or March.
 
• The festival is marked by ritualistic fasting, night-long vigils, and the chanting of Shiva mantras. Devotees visit Shiva temples to perform special pujas and offer milk, honey, and bilva (bael) leaves to the Shiva Lingam.
 
• Maha Shivaratri is believed to be the day when Shiva married Parvati or performed the Tandava, a cosmic dance of creation, preservation, and destruction. It is considered highly auspicious for spiritual growth, attracting devotees seeking the blessings for longevity and prosperity.
 
• The festival emphasizes self-restraint, meditation, and the purification of the mind and soul.
